page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware acceleration for AES and SHA cryptography.

Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, providing a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation that aligns more closely with compute-heavy profiles than standard 1:4 memory configurations. For high-speed local data caching and scratch space, the instance includes an integrated 945 GB NVMe SSD. GPU acceleration is absent with zero onboard graphics processors, and default allocations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2100.0 and stress-ng single-core scoring 3080.38, both situating the instance in the top quartile. Text processing and small-model lightweight LLM text generation also demonstrate upper-tier throughput. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks—such as Geekbench multi-core (12444.0) and stress-ng multi-core (24653.38)—deliver median results. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks tests in the lower quartile at 36.92 GB/sec, indicating a performance penalty during large contiguous read sweeps outside cache bounds.

The constrained memory footprint delivers strong resource efficiency for CPU-bound computations that do not justify paying for surplus RAM. With integrated local NVMe storage and solid single-thread throughput, the D16alds_v6 is suitable for static web serving, Clang compilation pipelines, batch text processing, continuous integration agents, and microservices requiring fast local disk IOPS.
description: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores at 3.7 GHz) using the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor and 32.0 GB of system memory. Designed with a compact 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, it integrates 945 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and crypto acceleration. Synthetic testing indicates upper-quartile single-core metrics in Geekbench and stress-ng, paired with average multi-threaded throughput and moderate memory bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPUs, the instance offers cost-efficient compute density by trimming surplus RAM overhead. It is suited for CI/CD compilation, text processing, microservices, and static web serving workloads requiring low-latency scratch storage.
